findings.title: The adaptive-default test bypasses the remote dispatch behavior it claims to guard
findings.detail: crates/blit-cli/tests/checker_pin_gate.rs:78 uses two local paths, but crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/mod.rs:794 exempts local routes from the checker-pin gate; the only remote checkers=0 assertion at mod.rs:872 calls the helper directly. I added a dispatch-only rejection of checkers=0 on non-local copy/mirror routes, and both added integration tests plus the modified unit test stayed green. A default remote transfer would therefore be rejected without these targeted guards noticing. Exercise a local-to-remote route with a guaranteed-missing temporary source, then assert the post-gate missing-source error rather than --checkers; that reaches the real remote dispatch without DNS or network I/O.

findings.title: The regression fixture can still resolve and write outside test-owned storage
findings.detail: crates/blit-cli/tests/checker_pin_gate.rs:35 assumes blit.invalid can never resolve and uses the fixed destination /tmp/blit-gate-dst. RFC 6761 controls DNS treatment, but system resolution can still honor a local hosts-file mapping. If the gate is removed, the copy case can consequently contact a live default-port daemon and populate that non-temporary destination—the same side-effect class this change is meant to eliminate. A missing local source paired with a remote destination fails before resolution after the gate and remains safe under the tested regression.
